name: isabelle-pide-stock
description: Isabelle proof assistant support for unmodified VS Code, driving `isabelle vscode_server` over LSP.

commands.title: Isabelle: Open Graph View in Editor

isabelle.autoStart.description: Start the language server when the extension activates. Turn this off to open .thy files without a prover -- symbol rendering, the outline and symbol input all work without one, and starting a session loads a heap image, which takes a while. Use "Isabelle: Start / Restart Language Server" when you want it.

isabelle.continuousChecking.description: Check the whole visible theory rather than a window around the caret (vscode_caret_perspective=0). Takes effect on server restart.

isabelle.expandAbbreviations.markdownDescription: Expand `\forall` into `\<forall>` as you type, and the short forms such as `\all`, `\ne`, `\iff`, `\_1` or `\[[` (caret inside `\<lbrakk>…\<rbrakk>`). Hover a symbol to see every way to type it.

isabelle.extendedServer.markdownDescription: Start Isabelle's language server with the additions this extension ships: the Query, Theories, Timing, Simplifier Trace and Graph View panels, Go to Command, and session images for `-R` that build. Your Isabelle installation is not modified. Available for Isabelle2025-2. Takes effect after reloading the window.

isabelle.input.customShorthands.markdownDescription: Your own `\` shorthands, added to the built-in ones and overriding them: `{"cup": "∪", "pair": "\\<langle>$CURSOR\\<rangle>"}` makes `\cup` type `\<union>`. Write the symbol as a glyph or as `\<name>`; the file always gets the ASCII escape. `$CURSOR` marks where the caret goes.

isabelle.graphview.description: Show the Graph View panel, which draws the output of thy_deps, class_deps, locale_deps and code_deps. The PIDE/graphview_* messages exist only on the vscode-graphview branch of mirror-isabelle.

isabelle.home.markdownDescription: Path to the Isabelle distribution (the directory containing `bin/isabelle`). Empty: use `$ISABELLE_HOME`, then well-known install locations.

isabelle.logic.description: Session image the language server boots with (isabelle vscode_server -l/-R). Imports already in this image load from a heap and are never re-checked; every other theory is elaborated from source on each start. The default "HOL" caches no project theory. Use "Isabelle: Select Session Image" to pick one from the ROOT files in the workspace.

isabelle.logicRequirements.markdownDescription: Start from an image built of `#isabelle.logic#`'s **requirements** (`-R`) rather than the session itself (`-l`). Use this when the theories you are editing belong to that session: everything they import is then loaded from a prebuilt heap and is never re-checked, while your own files stay live.
isabelle.logicRequirements.description: Boot with the chosen session's *requirements* (-R) rather than the session itself (-l). This is what you want while editing that session: everything it imports comes from a heap, while its own theories stay live and editable. With -l the session's own theories are in the image too, so they are not checked at all.

enumDescriptions: Colour checked text from the active colour theme, by serving PIDE markup as semantic tokens. Installing a theme then recolours the whole file.
Colour checked text from Isabelle's own text_color palette, as Isabelle/jEdit and the official Isabelle/VSCode do. The theme will not affect checked text.
isabelle.markupColors.markdownDescription: Who colours text that PIDE has checked. Processing status, message underlines and overview marks are unaffected either way. Note that `theme` relies on semantic highlighting, which `#editor.semanticHighlighting.enabled#` leaves to the theme by default; a theme that opts out falls back to the TextMate grammar.

isabelle.normalizeOnSave.markdownDescription: Before saving, rewrite any literal Unicode symbols back to `\<name>` escapes. `isabelle build` rejects literal Unicode, so this keeps files loadable.

isabelle.pideMarkup.markdownDescription: Apply PIDE markup (syntax colouring and processing status) as editor decorations.

isabelle.pideViewportScope.markdownDescription: Apply PIDE markup only to the visible part of the document (plus `#isabelle.renderMarginLines#`). The server sends markup for the whole file - over 51000 ranges on a 9000-line theory - and applying all of it costs roughly 40ms per keystroke. Disable only to compare against that behaviour.

isabelle.queryPanel.markdownDescription: Show the Query panel (find_theorems / find_consts). Requires an Isabelle whose language server exposes the `PIDE/query_*` messages; released versions do not. See the `vscode-query-panel` branch of mirror-isabelle.

isabelle.renderMarginLines.markdownDescription: How many lines above and below the viewport to decorate. Cost is linear in decorated ranges; keep the resulting count well under ~1500.

isabelle.renderSymbols.markdownDescription: Render `\<forall>`-style symbol escapes as Unicode glyphs using editor decorations. The file on disk stays ASCII.

isabelle.revealSymbolAtCursor.markdownDescription: Show the raw `\<name>` escape instead of the glyph for the symbol the cursor is inside, so it can be edited.

isabelle.serverArgs.description: Additional raw arguments appended to isabelle vscode_server.

isabelle.serverOptions.markdownDescription:
Isabelle system options passed as `-o NAME=VALUE`.

`vscode_pide_extensions` enables PIDE markup decorations and the Output/State panels. `vscode_html_output` makes those panels deliver HTML, and also avoids an Isabelle2025-2 bug where the non-HTML branch fails to serialise decorations. `vscode_unicode_symbols_output` renders glyphs in panels and hovers.

Do **not** enable `vscode_unicode_symbols_edits`: those edits are inserted into the buffer, which must stay ASCII.

isabelle.simplifierTrace.description: Show the Simplifier Trace panel. The PIDE/simplifier_trace_* messages exist only on the vscode-simplifier-trace branch of mirror-isabelle, so against a stock distribution this view would stay empty. Enable tracing with `declare [[simp_trace_new interactive mode=full]]` before the simp call, or `using [[simp_trace_new interactive mode=full]]` on the simp call itself.

isabelle.spellChecker.markdownDescription: Use Isabelle's own spell checker, which checks prose in comments and `text ‹…›` blocks by PIDE markup category (so antiquotations inside prose are excluded). Turn this off to avoid double underlining if you prefer a general spell-checking extension such as Code Spell Checker; the bundled TextMate grammar gives those extensions `comment.block.isabelle` and `string.quoted.*` scopes to target. Terms in `"…"` and `‹…›` are scoped as inner syntax, not as strings, so those extensions leave formulas alone.

isabelle.textColorOverrides.markdownDescription: Override individual PIDE markup colours, keyed `<name>_light` / `<name>_dark` (e.g. `keyword1_dark`). Defaults come from Isabelle's own palette.

isabelle.theoriesPanel.description: Show the Theories and Timing views. Requires the vscode-theories-panel branch of mirror-isabelle; a released Isabelle does not answer PIDE/theories_request.

isabelle.timingThreshold.description: Timing view: only commands at or above this many seconds are reported.

semanticTokenTypes.description: Isabelle command (lemma, definition, have, by, qed)
Isabelle minor keyword (where, and, fixes, shows) and `end`
Isabelle proof command that fixes, assumes or states a goal (fix, assume, obtain, case, show, thus)
Isabelle improper command (apply, done, prefer, defer)
Isabelle constant (a logical constant such as `map` or `Suc`)
